title: Rolling-price training completed; small general-price validation gain
question: Does dense price-only training establish useful forecasting compared with the previous event-only CNN training?
configuration: none+CNN~none~none on SPX-PX-GRID5-v1 (204,694 train) or SPX-PX-GRID15-v1 (68,219 train), common SPX-PX-GRID5-v1 validation (40,548), 35 historical bars, 20/30-minute returns, original five-minute processing lag, batch 64, AdamW 0.001, 30 epochs. One bounded single-GPU job planned.
finding: Both rolling-price fits completed 30 epochs (95,970 and 31,980 updates). Selected GRID15 CNN MAE on common 40,548-window rolling validation was 12.8773/15.8309 bp versus Persistence 12.9076/15.8647. Date-block intervals for these small gains exclude zero but do not adjust validation checkpoint selection. On the 149 matched Fed validation releases, neither selected fit improved over Persistence; all paired intervals span zero. Training losses continued downward while late validation error worsened.
limitations: Exploratory validation used for checkpoint and stride comparison; intervals condition on selected fits. Overlapping rolling windows are correlated. Dense training changes population, fitted scaling and selection population together. Price timing assumptions remain. No text arm or reserved-test scoring.

figure.alt: Full training loss and common rolling-validation MAE through 30 epochs for five- and fifteen-minute training strides.
